#1649. Four clubs Bruno Fernandes could join after Man Utd captain rejects new contract offer

By Matthew Cooper | 13 Nov 2026 12:29, Last updated: 13 Nov 2026 12:31

Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has reportedly rejected a second contract offer from the club, raising further questions about his long-term future at Old Trafford.

The Portugal international's current agreement expires in June 2027, although United do have the option to extend it by a further 12 months.

However, with the two parties yet to reach an agreement, the possibility of Fernandes ultimately moving on has increased.

Fernandes has previously spoken about his ambitions beyond Manchester, expressing an interest in moving to Spain and returning to Italy or Portugal.

Given the fresh uncertainty over his future, Sports Mole has taken a look at four clubs Fernandes could join.

A return to Sporting CP would be the most emotional option for Fernandes, who established himself as one of Europe's most influential midfielders during his time in Lisbon.

The Portuguese international scored 63 goals in 137 appearances for Sporting after joining from Sampdoria in 2017, becoming captain and winning the Portuguese League Cup and Portuguese Cup before moving to Old Trafford in January 2020.

In an interview with Canal 11 last year, Fernandes admitted a return to Sporting appealed to him, stating: "I've thought about returning to Portugal.

"Going back to where you were once happy can tarnish the image you have left. Out of affection and respect, my first choice would be Sporting.

"But I don't want to spoil the beautiful image I have. Even for family reasons, I would like to return to Portugal. But I don't want to go there only for what I did but because I can add something."

Fernandes has a long history with Italian football, having represented Novara, Udinese and Sampdoria before moving to Sporting.

He has previously spoken about a potential return to Italy, stating: "I have many links to the country. My daughter was born there and she keeps saying that she wants to learn Italian and if I could provide that and play for a club in Italy that has big aims and fight for a chance to win titles, it's an idea that like."

A team like Juventus, the most successful club in Italy, would certainly fit the bill and they have previously been linked with the Portuguese playmaker.

Juventus have also struggled in recent years, having not won a Serie A title since 2020, and would surely benefit from the addition of a player like Fernandes.

Atletico Madrid could offer Fernandes the opportunity to play in Spain, which is another of his stated ambitions.

Atletico would represent an attractive destination given they regularly challenge Real Madrid and Barcelona in La Liga and are a constant presence in the Champions League.

Fernandes' creativity, intensity and ability to operate in several midfield roles could make him an appealing signing for Diego Simeone.

Al Hilal represent a very different proposition, having already demonstrated their willingness to spend heavily in an attempt to bring Fernandes to Saudi Arabia.

The Saudi Pro League side reportedly made an offer worth around £100m to Manchester United in 2025, while Fernandes was understood to have been offered wages of up to £700,000 per week.

Despite the financial appeal, the Portuguese international rejected the opportunity, explaining: "The president of Al Hilal called me a month ago to ask... But I simply want to stay at the highest level, playing in the big competitions, because I still feel capable of that."

However, Al Hilal remain admirers of Fernandes and another approach could prove difficult to turn down given the finances involved.

#1648. Opinion: Liverpool will sign their next Fabinho if they make move for €50m midfielder

Fabinho left Liverpool in 2023 and they still haven't properly replaced him.

When the Brazilian was initially brought in, his transfer was a complete surprise.

It felt like fans had just woken up one day and, all of a sudden, they had a new defensive midfielder in town.

The five years that the midfielder spent at Anfield were excellent. He won every trophy possible and was a key cog in Jurgen Klopp's system.

However, after his form dropped off, the Reds were quick to move him on with many fans believing that this was because they'd have a replacement lined up.

Evidently, that wasn't the case as, even though Fabinho was sold in July 2023, Liverpool still haven't replaced him, but, that could all be about to change.

Angelo Stiller is ready to leave VFB Stuttgart as soon as possible

Defensive midfield has been a major issue for Liverpool over the last couple of years.

No matter who the Reds try and use there, things just don't quite work out.

Recently, Alexis Mac Allister and Trey Nyoni have been Andoni Iraola's preferred options but, since Mac Allister isn't a natural number six and Nyoni is still only 19 years old, neither of them are the best possible options for Liverpool to have.

So, that's why this latest update from Florian Plettenberg is something that could excite the Reds' fanbase.

"Angelo Stiller and his agency, Sports360, have parted ways by mutual consent. However, the initiative came from the agency, with differing views on the player’s future," he shared via X.

"Stiller is once again very open to a move. Saudi Arabia, MLS and Türkiye are also options. Contract with VfB Stuttgart valid until 2028."

Angelo Stiller could become Liverpool's next Fabinho

A completely natural number six is a rare thing to find in football these days.

Most defensive midfielders try their best to cover every single aspect of being a midfielder and, in the end, none of them end up with a specialised position.

But, with how attacking Iraola's tactics are, Liverpool are a team who need a natural number six that can defend and help keep their back line solid.

Angelo Stiller has been on the Reds' radar for some time now with the Reds and Real Madrid both being linked in the past.

A fee worth around €50 million (£41.7 million) is what would be required to prise him from the Bundesliga outfit which, with how good he is, feels like an absolute steal.

The German has played in 328 games across his career so far despite only being 25 years old.

This experience coupled with his defensive capability are the two reasons why Stiller could be the Reds' new Fabinho.

Obviously, the fact that interest in the midfielder has died down recently also plays in Liverpool's favour and could mean that they get a few more million knocked off the deal which would be even better. Here's hoping that a deal is struck soon.

Or that Liverpool at least re-ignite their interest in signing him.

#1647. Norway vs. Wales: Erling Haaland plan revealed by Craig Bellamy ahead of key UEFA Nations League clash

By Darren Plant | 13 Nov 2026 12:42

Craig Bellamy has revealed his plan to stop Erling Haaland as Wales square off against Norway on Saturday evening.

With two matches remaining, Wales make the trip to Norway sitting level on points with their upcoming opponents in Group A4.

As a result of Wales winning the reverse fixture in Cardiff, they will guarantee at least third place in the group with another victory.

Although Wales prevented Haaland from scoring in that contest, the Manchester City star boasts an incredible record of 65 goals from 59 appearances for his country.

During his pre-match press conference, Bellamy was naturally quizzed on how he wants Wales to play against Haaland.

While Bellamy admitted that adopting a specific strategy was "easier said than done", he was clear that he wants his players to repeat what they did in the first game.

He told reporters: "Drive up and don't let him dictate It's easier said than done. You can't have him dictating the game. That's true of all players, really, but it's much harder when someone is getting in your face and stopping you from having time on the ball.

"It's a collective responsibility, not just an individual one. You have to consider the distance between Ethan [Ampadu] and Haaland.

"You can't open up the middle too much because balls are going to come into his feet. You have to get your distances right, be side-on, and make sure you're aware of his runs.

"He has the ability to take a team on, but he also has the willingness to make those runs.

"It's also important how we use the ball. If we use it well, develop our possession and move up the pitch, he has to work. He has to run and get back."

If Wales can avoid defeat in Norway, it would force Stale Solbakken's side to avoid losing in Denmark on matchday six to not finish bottom of the group.

Should Wales lose to Norway by a two-goal margin, relegation to League B would be confirmed due to their inferior head-to-head records against Norway and Denmark.

#1646. USMNT fans in meltdown as head coach Mauricio Pochettino emerges as frontrunner for Manchester United job

By DANIEL MATTHEWS, US SENIOR SPORTS WRITER

Published: 21:47 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 23:51 EST, 9 November 2026

US soccer fans were sent into a frenzy on Monday by the news that Mauricio Pochettino is in pole position to join Manchester United.

As reported by the Daily Mail, Michael Carrick is facing the sack with United bosses leaning towards hiring a new coach during the international break.

Pochettino has emerged as a frontrunner for the role, despite signing a new contract following the World Cup, when he led the USMNT to the last 16.

The Argentine committed his future to the end of the next World Cup in 2030 but his contract includes a £7 million ($9.4 million) release clause. And news of Manchester United's interest left many USMNT fans fearing the worst.

'[That] was fun while it lasted!' one said. 'Wow - just when you thought things had settled a bit with the USMNT!' added a second, while a third said: 'Noooo they can’t have our coach!'

Many other supporters on social media refused to believe that Pochettino could leave but his future has been under the microscope ever since he took over in September 2024.

Mauricio Pochettino is in pole position to replace Michael Carrick at Manchester United

Carrick is facing the sack with United leaning towards hiring a new coach in the coming weeks

The 54-year-old Pochettino has made no secret of his desire to return to the Premier League

The 54-year-old has made no secret of his desire to return to the Premier League, while it emerged ahead of the World Cup that he had held discussions with AC Milan.

Pochettino's team sparkled en route to the last 16, only to crash out against Belgium after President Trump's intervention over the red card shown to striker Folarin Balogun.

His initial contract expired after the tournament but after weeks of uncertainty, the former Chelsea, Tottenham and Southampton coach signed a four-year extension.

He is slated to take charge of a Nations League double-header against Haiti during this international break, with a press conference set for Friday.

Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann, who were both under consideration when United gave Carrick more time to turn the season around following a 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth last month, could also be in contention.

#1645. £380m = zero points: Big-spending Spurs humbled by Newcastle

These remain the earliest of early days but the blunt facts are there for all to see. Tottenham Hotspur, the club that has spent around £380m this summer in search of instant improvements, have played twice and lost twice in the Premier League. After making eight new signings, they have so far scored zero goals and won zero points.

Not since 1974 has a Spurs team lost the first two games of a league campaign without finding the net. The summer enthusiasm in this corner of north London is therefore already drifting away, to the sound of an alarmingly familiar soundtrack: boos from the home supporters at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

This meeting with Newcastle United was, in the minds of those Spurs fans, meant to be a clash between a team remade by the transfer market and a team broken by it. Yet it was Newcastle, still adjusting to the loss of three key players this summer, who looked the more unified group and more organised team.

It proved to be a truly glorious evening for the visiting supporters, who not only delighted in their team’s victory but also in the struggles of Sandro Tonali. The £100m Italian, who swapped Newcastle for Spurs a few weeks ago, never came close to offering the sort of class one would expect for such a fee. That price tag is not his fault but it is his burden, and in time he will need to shoulder it more impressively than he did here.

Roberto De Zerbi, the Spurs head coach, can rightly say that it will take time for his new group to develop the cohesion he needs. The worrying reality for Spurs, though, is that his opposite number had far less time to work with his players and far less money to reshape his squad. Matthias Jaissle appears to be a man with a defined plan, and an ability to convey it. Newcastle improved considerably after half-time, which spoke volumes of Jaissle’s work. “He is the best signing of Newcastle so far,” said Yoane Wissa of his new coach.

"He is the best signing for Newcastle"Yoane Wissa praises Matthias Jaissle's impact at the club since becoming head coach 👔 pic.twitter.com/dX8nVknpKc

For Spurs, so much of it would have felt painfully similar to last season, when they won only three home games in the Premier League. They played some pretty football in bursts, but not at the crucial points of the game. The second half, especially, was pockmarked with moments of despair. There was Mathys Tel’s free-kick that almost flew into Islington, for example, and Mateus Fernandes falling over when running onto a pass in the penalty area.

De Zerbi said he was sorry for the fans and for the club, and suggested his team is not properly prepared for this campaign. “Maybe we are not ready yet,” he said. “For many, many reasons we are not ready yet.”

"I have no panic, I know very well where I'm going" Roberto De Zerbi apologises to Spurs fans after the defeat to Newcastle 🔊 pic.twitter.com/83DntjG5ZH

Newcastle’s two goals, much like Brentford’s three last weekend, exposed the enduring frailties in the Spurs defence. Anthony Elanga’s opener stemmed from a long pass over the top of the home side’s high line, while Wissa’s acrobatic effort came from a corner kick that Spurs could not handle. Neither strike, it would be safe to say, was the result of world-class attacking play.

Anthony Elanga finishes brilliantly and celebrates just as Thierry Henry did against Spurs 💥 pic.twitter.com/l6qndlMrKm

What a GOAL from Yoane Wissa?! 🫨 pic.twitter.com/mjuHpaa4YY

“After the first goal we lost confidence,” said De Zerbi. “The reaction was not good enough, not what I want to see on the pitch. The solution is not to put the head down, but to react.”

To be clear, Spurs were not quite as bad as they had been against Brentford on the opening day. They did create chances here, taking 17 shots and forcing a few terrific saves from Lukas Hornicek, Newcastle’s impressive goalkeeper. But in the key moments they suffered from the same absence of clarity and execution as they did last season. Troublingly, this seemed to affect the new signings as much as it did the longer-serving players.

Of the five new arrivals who featured for Spurs, Tonali was the least effective. The Italian had been vigorously booed by the away fans before kick-off and the travelling Geordies waited with palpable excitement for his first mistake. Much to their delight, it arrived after only three minutes: an underhit pass, in his own half, which directly led to Micky van de Ven picking up a yellow card. Tonali was outshone by new Newcastle midfielder Nico Gonzalez, who excelled only a few days after completing his move from Manchester City.

"He's got an opportunity to be the main man"Jamie Redknapp praises Nico Gonzalez's performance on his debut 👏 pic.twitter.com/1ga3tsxXHA

Might it have been different for Spurs if £75m winger Savio had been available? The Brazilian was electrifying on his debut in midweek, when he scored against Charlton Athletic in the League Cup, yet was unavailable here due to a minor injury. It instead fell to another signing from City, Omar Marmoush, to lead the attack. He was busy and floaty but never truly hurt Newcastle.

There are more changes to come at Spurs before Tuesday’s deadline. De Zerbi revealed after the game that Richarlison, Kevin Danso and Pape Matar Sarr have all asked to leave the club.

At least the issues facing his players appear clear to De Zerbi. His list of areas to improve was lengthy – he spoke of strengthening the connection between the players, the quality of their play, their work in the defensive phase and the distances between them – but he also insisted he loves them and remains confident in the club’s project. At this rate, though, the fans might not share that confidence for much longer.

The Tottenham boss told BBC Sport: “Disappointed for the result because until the first goal we conceded I think we played better than Newcastle. We lost ball possession in the first half because we didn’t defend in the right way, the distance between the defenders and attackers was too big. We can improve in the defensive phases but today was an unfair result.

“At the beginning of the second half we had some chance to create the potential chances. We created many chances to score, we have to improve the last decision, because that will make a difference. At the end we are disappointed for the result and our fans. We are working to be a great team. When we become a team I think we can change the story of the last two seasons for Tottenham.

“We are working to be good on the pitch, if you believe in work and training then you have to improve day by day.”

Speaking to Sky Sports, Newcastle’s head coach said: “It was incredible and I’m really proud. We are really proud as a club, as a coaching staff to see a team on the pitch delivering the match plan at a high level already, but also seeing players fully committed to what we’re doing. This is a good start and a moment to enjoy.

“We also did well last week against Liverpool, therefore it was a step in the right direction again against a strong opponent with huge signings during the transfer window. This is something we were aware of, but how we handled that challenge was amazing.”

"He is the best signing for Newcastle"Yoane Wissa praises Matthias Jaissle's impact at the club since becoming head coach 👔 pic.twitter.com/dX8nVknpKc

"With the fans behind us, no one can stop us" 🖤Yoane Wissa reacts to Newcastle's win at Spurs! pic.twitter.com/itaiVO3Kx1

After a tumultuous summer, Jaissle has ushered in a new era of hope and positivity at Newcastle, with Wissa and Elanga reborn in attack.

"Oh Jaissle, I can boogie..." 🎶🕺 pic.twitter.com/FmvC2DrLMO

2 - Anthony Elanga is the first player to score in both of Newcastle United's first two Premier League games of a campaign since Alan Shearer in 2003-04.Footsteps. pic.twitter.com/VZ3hXEbpG7

2 - Tottenham Hotspur have lost their opening two matches of a league campaign without scoring for the first time since the 1974-75 season.Concerning. pic.twitter.com/N8izpVYslx

Jaissle records his first ever Premier League win, heaping more misery upon Tottenham, who begin the season with two defeats. Excellent second-half finishes from Elanga and Wissa have given the visitors a superb three points in the capital.

YOU MAGSSSS! 🤩 pic.twitter.com/PRM8yYg7Yl

Barnes attempts to latch onto a ball in behind, but Kinsky races out to claim. Spurs then almost half-heartedly come forward as Udogie tries to find Marmoush with a powerful cross. The new Spurs forward gets some contact on the ball, but it ricochets to Hall, who hacks it clear. Newcastle then make a late change as Toure replaces Barnes.

Fernandes clips a pinpoint cross into Marmoush. The Egyptian shoots via a first-time volley, but his tame attempt is easily gathered by Hornicek.

Van de Ven’s reintegration into Spurs’ defence hasn’t proved helpful. The hosts have been all at sea at the back since the restart. Newcastle showed little attacking ambition in the first half but have ripped Tottenham apart in the second.

Jaissle makes another double change as both goal-scorers, Elanga and Wissa, are taken off for Murphy and Ramsey. Elanga and Wissa have both produced extremely positive displays to kickstart their seasons under their new head coach.

Spurs have looked way off the pace in this second half and Newcastle are well worth their lead on the basis of their performance since the break.

The away fans sarcastically cheer as Tonali is withdrawn for Solanke. The former Newcastle midfielder has struggled against his old club, drastically failing to impact the game.

The visitors are in dreamland! Hall swings in a corner and Woltemade towers above Udogie to win the header. The ball breaks to Wissa, who fires a delightful acrobatic finish into the net, extending Newcastle’s advantage. Spurs’ crisis deepens. They’re on course for two defeats to start the season.

What a GOAL from Yoane Wissa?! 🫨 pic.twitter.com/mjuHpaa4YY

And this time it is another two of last summer’s signings who have combined for Newcastle United’s second goal of the afternoon.

Nick Woltemade won the initial header and got the assist a few seconds after replacing Joe Willock, but what a finish from Yoane Wissa, an improvised overhead flick from close range.

Newcastle needed Elanga and Wissa to be far better this season than they were in their first campaign on Tyneside and both of them have been electric so far under Matthias Jaissle.

As for Sandro Tonali, Newcastle saw this version of the Italy international all too often in his final season at St James’ Park. Good engine, runs around a lot, but does not influence the game in any meaningful way. A reminder Spurs spent £100m on him and have spent almost £400m in total this summer. They have been abject in the second half.

Porro tries his luck from range but Hornicek is there for Newcastle to tip the ball over the bar. The visitors then make a double change as Steur and Woltemade replace Nico and Willock.

De Zerbi makes a triple change as Spurs look to find a way back into this match. Robertson, Gray and Tel depart for Udogie, Moore and Kudus.

Spurs have a free kick in a dangerous position, but Tel slips as he goes to shoot and it flies well over the bar. That sums up Tottenham’s evening so far.

That makes two goals in two games for Elanga, who scored zero Premier League goals last season. It’s an outstanding finish, on the spin while falling backwards. It prompted some great noises from the away end, too, as the ball seemed to cross the line in slow motion.

The visitors have started his second half well and fly into the lead. Nico switches the play and picks out Dedic with a precise long-ball. The full-back cushions a header into Elanga, who swivels and slides a low effort in off the post to open the scoring and send the away support into a euphoric sea of celebration. What answers do Spurs and De Zerbi have now?

Anthony Elanga finishes brilliantly and celebrates just as Thierry Henry did against Spurs 💥 pic.twitter.com/l6qndlMrKm

Newcastle deserved that goal. They have been the stronger side since the halftime interval, and this is the Anthony Elanga that Eddie Howe thought he was signing last summer.

He scored on the opening weekend against Liverpool, but this was an even better finish, spinning sharply and sweeping a shot home on the turn. Smart dance moves for the celebration too.

It all came about from another long diagonal ball forward, but this time it was inch perfect from Nico Gonzalez for Harvey Barnes to put a header into the path of Elanga inside the box.

Newcastle are really growing into this contest, with Spurs getting deeper and deeper. Elanga is starting to get some joy out wide.

The momentum has arguably been with Newcastle since the interval. They’re pushing Spurs back towards their own goal. The visitors are waiting to fashion a real big chance.

Elanga latches onto Hall’s pass, gets in behind Spurs’ defence and beats Kinsky to the ball. However, it was a difficult pass to control and his touch is too heavy, causing the opportunity to disappear. Newcastle are certainly looking more adventurous at the start of this second half.

The visitors make a rare foray forward as Hall bends an ambitious curler from long range that flies off target. That is more encouraging for Newcastle.

Early drama at the start of this half as Spurs appeal for a penalty. Thiaw and Marmoush challenge for a 50-50. The Tottenham forward crashes to the floor as the Newcastle captain goes for the clearance. The referee’s on-field decision is no penalty and VAR agrees. After seeing the replays, there wasn’t too much contact and it would have been a harsh penalty if given.

We are back under way for the second half. Will we see a goal at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium this evening?

Spurs have been knocking on the door and looked like the far more threatening side, but they’ve been unable to find an opening goal. Newcastle have defended diligently and frustrated their opponents. However, in forward areas, they look disjointed and are lacking serious firepower.

⏸️ @SpursOfficial 0-0 @NUFC There's nothing to separate the two sides at half-time pic.twitter.com/ICFqQ3eXMO

Tel has drifted out to the right wing and turns inside of Nico before whipping a ball into the box which narrowly evades Marmoush. Tonali then bursts forward and passes to Porro, but Hall thwarts Spurs’ latest attack by blocking the makeshift winger’s shot.

I would be worried if I were Matthias Jaissle. Newcastle have not looked comfortable dealing with Tottenham’s corners and goalkeeper Lukasz Hornicek has made a couple of good saves this half to keep the scores level.

Much of Newcastle’s attacking play has been aimless, with long diagonal balls pumped forward that the Tottenham defence is prepared for and has tended to deal with easily.

Very little is happening in midfield and neither Joe Willock in the number 10 role nor Yoane Wissa at centre forward has had any real joy in the final third.

It all looks a bit predictable going forward and, if we are being ultra critical, a bit aimless too. They have not forced a save from the Spurs goalkeeper as we approach half time.

Marmoush has become far more involved over the last ten minutes and has showcased his quality with a few notable touches and darting runs. Nevertheless, Spurs have been unable to breach Newcastle’s stubborn defence.

A free-flowing Tottenham move involving Van Hecke and Marmoush ends with Porro sliding a low cross in towards the unmarked Tel at the back post. The Spaniard doesn’t quite can’t enough power on the delivery and Hornicek rushes out to collect.

Marmoush slips a clever pass through to Robertson, who fires in a first-time cross which flies out for a corner. Fernandes whips a corner into the box and Van Hecke wins the header, beating two Newcastle players to the ball. But Hornicek is there to parry the Dutchman’s close-range header away.

Robertson’s deep corner finds an unmarked Marmoush at the back stick. He takes a first-time shot, but his volley bounces wide of the near post. From that range, he needs to be getting that on target.

Marmoush has been on the periphery so far today. Spurs have looked threatening but they could be more attentive with possession at times, especially in midfield.

Van de Ven makes a crucial challenge to stop Wissa from fashioning a shooting opportunity inside the six-yard box after good build-up play from Nico and Elanga.

Newcastle are trying to get the ball forward quickly in this new “vertical” style of Matthias Jaissle but all it is doing at the moment is give it straight back to Tottenham Hotspur.

It has not been a fun first 20 minutes to watch from the visitors who have had little joy breaking through the lines and have invited pressure from Spurs.

The less said about their set piece delivery the better. Harvey Barnes has taken over corner duties from Bruno Guimaraes and has not managed to clear the first Tottenham defender yet.

Tottenham play a short corner and Botman’s headed clearance only finds Porro, who is lurking on the edge of Newcastle’s penalty area. Porro’s catches the ball on the volley, but his strike flies over. The World Cup winner is playing with real confidence.

Jan Paul van Hecke has played a couple of exceptional forward passes in the early exchanges here. The £52m signing is already demonstrating his ability to start attacks from deep.

The Tottenham Hotspur Stadium screams for a free kick as Porro believes he was brought down by Willock on the edge of the penalty area. There’s minimal contact and referee Peter Bankes is not interested, waving play on.

Tottenham stream into Newcastle’s penalty area, and Tonali’s miscued makes it way through to Porro. He feints to send Miley flying, but Hall is there to make a goal-saving block and thwart Porro’s attempt. Spurs are beginning to grow into this contest and are currently in the ascendency.

Tel forces a flying save from Hornicek! Van Hecke picks out Marmoush with a piercing pass through Newcastle’s midfield, allowing the former Manchester Ciy man to tee up Tel. The winger takes the ball in his stride, cuts inside and whips a venomous effort at goal. Hornicek is up to the task and dives to make the stop.

Tonali has made an unsettled start to this game. He’s already given possession away on a couple of occasions and left space for Newcastle to exploit.

Nico then receives a yellow card on his Newcastle debut for apprehending Gray to stop Tottenham from counter-attacking.

Tonali and Tel give away the ball, allowing Newcastle to attack. Wissa cushions Dedic’s cross with an exquisite touch for Barnes, but the winger curls his effort comfortably off target and fails to trouble Kinsky.

Marmoush has been deployed as the central striker on his Tottenham debut, with Fernandes just behind him as the most advanced midfielder. Porro also looks to be starting on the right wing. It’s a very new-look frontline for Spurs following last weekend’s defeat to Brentford.

Sandro Tonali’s first meaningful action: badly underhitting a simple pass to Micky van de Ven. It resulted in the Spurs captain picking up a yellow card. The Newcastle fans are singing a song about Tonali in the away end, but I won’t repeat the lyrics here.

Tonali under-hits a pass back to Van de Ven, who flies in with a late challenge on Wissa, needlessly colliding with the Newcastle forward. The Spurs captain picks up an early booking. That it not the start he would have wanted.

Newcastle threaten straight away as Elanga nearly lifts an audacious lob over Kinsky from a tight angle. It doesn’t quite squeeze into the bottom corner and Spurs get back to concede a corner inside the first minute. Fernandes then bumps into Dedic off the ball, giving the visitors a free kick.

We are under way in North London. Can either side record their first Premier League win of the season after midweek Carabao Cup victories?

Captains Van de Ven and Thiaw lead their respective sides out onto the pitch. The Tottenham Hotspur Stadium is in full voice, with kick-off just minutes away.

With just under ten minutes until kick-off, here’s a recap of the two line-ups this evening.

Tottenham: Kinsky; Gray, Van Hecke, Van de Ven, Robertson; Bentancur, Tonali; Porro, Fernandes, Tel; Marmoush.

Subs: Dubravka, Senesi, Gallagher, Udogie, Bergvall, Solanke, Kudus, Davies, Moore.

Newcastle: Hornicek; Dedic, Thiaw, Botman, Hall; Miley, Gonzalez; Elanga, Willock, Barnes; Wissa.

Subs: Jaouen, Schar, Bamba, Steur, Toure, Murphy, Woltemade, Ramsey, Shahar.

Roberto De Zerbi has explained Sávio's absence from our matchday squad ℹ️📲 https://t.co/ACZscgieFg pic.twitter.com/ddGz2NveX3

“It was bad news yesterday before training in the afternoon because he suffered muscle fatigue and the medical staff obviously didn’t want to take a risk and I agree with them - it’s not the right moment, especially because he didn’t work in the last 10 days, for him 20 minutes against Charlton, maybe it was tough to rest for the days after but for the next game I think there are no problems.”

"Quality." 🤷‍♂️Matthias Jaissle on what Nico González adds to the Newcastle side 💬 pic.twitter.com/yjMBcr0pUm

"If I'm a Tottenham fan, this is the most excited I've been in MANY YEARS"Jamie Redknapp thinks that Spurs have built a strong squad that can compete in the Premier League 👀 pic.twitter.com/55Dwm7BaoE

It is not the sight of their former player Sandro Tonali in a Tottenham Hotspur shirt that will worry Newcastle United.

Omar Marmoush was only at Manchester City for 18 months but managed to score seven goals in just five appearances against Newcastle, including a hat-trick back in February 2025.

The Egyptian has moved to Spurs seeking regular first team football and will go up against the team he has enjoyed facing more than any other in English football.

Newcastle, of course, have a new manager Matthias Jaissle and are playing a different style of football under the German. Despite an unbeaten start in league and cup, the defence has not looked particularly assured.

That could make the ideal opponents for Spurs as they look to prove last season’s miserable home form is not going to continue into this one.

I’m fascinated to see how Newcastle play here. They were happy to sit back, soak up pressure and go direct in attack, mainly on the counter. That sort of approach could be even more effective away from home than at St James’ Park.

For me, it is far too early to say a summer of change has worked for Newcastle. We will have a better idea after this game.

Sandro Tonali’s departure from Newcastle United did not provoke the same extreme anger as Alexander Isak’s acrimonious move to Liverpool or the sadness of captain Bruno Guimarães’ switch to Arsenal. That is largely because nobody will miss him as much.

There is no doubt the Italy international’s determination to leave for Tottenham Hotspur did rankle supporters, especially given the club had stood by him during a 10-month betting ban, but Tonali was only a good player for Newcastle, not a great one.

Nico will make his NUFC debut today 🤩 pic.twitter.com/ilEM8w3Dwd

Roberto De Zerbi has said that Savio is missing because of “muscle fatigue.”

Tottenham had been hoping to see Savinho following his glittering cameo which yielded a goal and an assist against Charlton on Wednesday, but they will have to wait for his Premier League debut.

Both of these teams signed players from Manchester City this week. Omar Marmoush joined Spurs on a loan with a £60m obligation, while Nico Gonzalez moved to Newcastle for £52m. Both players have been thrown straight into the starting lineups of their respective teams.

Tottenham: Kinsky; Gray, Van Hecke, Van de Ven, Robertson; Bentancur, Tonali; Porro, Fernandes, Tel; Marmoush.

Subs: Dubravka, Senesi, Gallagher, Udogie, Bergvall, Solanke, Kudus, Davies, Moore.

Newcastle: Hornicek; Dedic, Thiaw, Botman, Hall; Miley, Gonzalez; Elanga, Willock, Barnes; Wissa.

Subs: Jaouen, Schar, Bamba, Steur, Toure, Murphy, Woltemade, Ramsey, Shahar.

Recent recruit Nico Gonzalez begins in midfield and is set to make his Newcastle debut. Joe Willock scored in the Liverpool draw and is rewarded with a start, replacing the injured Will Osula.

Nico's in from the start! 🙌 pic.twitter.com/wx28WChueB

Unsurprisingly, Roberto De Zerbi has made five changes to the team that wilted against Brentford.

Marcos Senesi, Lucas Bergvall, Conor Gallagher, Mikey Moore and Richarlison have been dropped. In come Micky van de Ven, who captains the side, Rodrigo Bentancur, Pedro Porro, Mateus Fernandes and Omar Marmoush. Savinho is missing altogether.

Good evening from the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, where there is no sign of new Spurs winger Savio. After his thrilling debut against Charlton Athletic in midweek, the £75m forward seems to have picked up an injury. We’ll learn the reason for his absence very soon.

As expected, Sandro Tonali starts in the Spurs midfield. His second Premier League game for his new club comes against his former team. There’s also a start for new man Omar Marmoush, who is making his first appearance for Spurs following his move from City.

Our Spurs side to face Newcastle! 🤍🔢 @krakenfx pic.twitter.com/djFKnl6nsi

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League meeting between Tottenham and Newcastle United in North London.

Following consecutive 17th-place finishes in the last two seasons, Spurs are looking to enjoy a fresh start under Roberto De Zerbi without nervously looking over their shoulder at the perilous possibility of relegation.

Nevertheless, Spurs’ season started disastrously last weekend as they fell to a miserable 3-0 defeat against Brentford at the Gtech Community Stadium. Since that result, Spurs have responded with an emphatic 5-1 thrashing of Charlton Athletic in the Carabao Cup, and also confirmed the signings of Savinho and Omar Marmoush from Manchester City. De Zerbi will be looking to continue this newfound momentum in the club’s first top-flight home match of the 2026-27 campaign.

Newcastle United have undergone a summer of significant change. Eddie Howe stepped down as head coach after nearly five years in charge, while Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes and Anthony Gordon all departed the club for lucrative transfer fees. Tonali welcomes his former employers to his new surroundings after joining Tottenham for £100m.

Despite this upheaval, Newcastle demonstrated admirable heart in new boss Matthias Jaissle’s first game in charge, earning a hard-fought 2-2 draw with Liverpool at St. James’ Park on the opening weekend. Emotional tributes poured in for club legend Kevin Keegan as Alexander Isak made his return to the club he acrimoniously forced an exit from last summer.

Newcastle looked to be heading for a victory after goals from Anthony Elanga and Joe Willock, until Lewis Hall, who had played excellently, apprehended Liverpool substitute Victor Munoz in added time to concede a penalty. Dominik Szoboszlai smashed a clinical spot-kick into the top corner to rescue a point for the visitors. Newcastle bounced back from these dropped points with a tense 3-2 triumph over West Brom in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday evening.

A first Premier League win of the season is the aim for both clubs by the end of this evening.

Kick-off is at 17:30, with team news on the way shortly.

Alexandre Pato is one of the greatest ‘What If’ players of his generation and AC Milan will always hold him in high regard.

For many, even non-Milan fans, Pato is one of the defining players of the ‘What If’ term. The Brazilian had everything required to make him a modern great. Fantastic in front of goal, skilful, fun and genuinely exciting, he seemed like a potential world beater.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

With the Rossoneri, there are only fond memories and he’s one that most will have loved growing up.

However, his record with injuries prevented him from ever becoming the player that most hoped he’d be one day. Yet, the relationship never soured and he remains a fan favourite, even to this day.

Speaking to Luca Toni for the Prime special Fenomeni column, Pato responded to some questions about his injury troubles and one encounter with Alessandro Nesta in the dressing room, as MilanNews relays.

“I remember that after yet another injury, Nesta came into the locker room furious and said I shouldn’t have played. I have enormous respect for AC Milan, who gave me everything, but perhaps that moment could have been handled better.

“One of the things that hurt me the most, and which I’ve never spoken about before, was hearing people at the club say I’d never play again. That was sad, especially because as players, we know that a club is like a company, and if you don’t play, someone else comes in to replace you.

“At that time, I couldn’t speak out, especially because I was young and didn’t understand. With today’s mentality, I’d handle myself differently.”

#1643. Latvia vs Armenia - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ellis Stevens | 13 Nov 2026 13:33

Latvia will welcome Armenia to Stadions Skonto on Sunday afternoon for the final clash in UEFA Nations League C Group 2.

Both teams' positions in the standings have already been confirmed, with the hosts destined to finish at the bottom of the table and the visitors guaranteed to finish third.

Latvia have endured a miserable 2026-27 UEFA Nations League campaign, failing to secure a single victory and picking up just one point from their five fixtures to date.

Paolo Nicolato's side are, therefore, guaranteed to finish bottom of the standings, as they are unable to make up the four-point gap to third-placed Armenia with only one game remaining.

However, Latvia will be spared relegation from League C due to the restructuring of the competition into a three-league system for the 2028-29 edition, meaning all third and fourth-placed finishers will retain their status in League C.

Regardless, Nicolato will be desperate for his side to avoid finishing an entire campaign without claiming a victory, while also looking to end Latvia's seven-game unbeaten run across all competitions - since defeating Gibraltar in back-to-back matches to ensure they avoided relegation to League D in March 2026.

Latvia have shown signs of improvement in recent matches, scoring in each of their last three games after initially failing to find the net in their opening two, although they have conceded two goals in each of those three defeats.

The hosts were also defeated comfortably by Armenia in the reverse fixture on matchday one, with Georgiy Harutyunyan and Artur Gharibyan finding the back of the net either side of half-time to secure all three points for Sunday's visitors.

That victory was the last time Armenia emerged victorious, however, as Yeghishe Melikyan's side have subsequently recorded two defeats and two draws.

Those results leave Armenia third in the table heading into the final fixture, and while they trail second-placed Cyprus by only three points, their inferior head-to-head record means they are unable to climb up the standings.

Armenia, since losing to Cyprus on matchday three, have remained unbeaten in their last two games, recording back-to-back draws, and they will be looking to build on those results with another win against Latvia on Sunday.

Alongside winning 2-0 in the reverse fixture in September, Armenia have also won four of the last five clashes with Latvia, including all of the last three encounters.

Armenia have scored at least two goals in all of their last four victories over Latvia, with the exception being a 2-0 defeat in Latvia in October 2023.

Deniss Melniks scored Latvia's only goal in the 2-1 defeat to Montenegro earlier this week, and the defender should continue alongside Antonijs Cernomordijs and Oskars Vientiess.

Further forward, Andrejs Ciganiks and Eduards Daskevics should provide the width in attacking areas, with Roberts Uldrikis leading the line.

Meanwhile, Gharibyan scored his second goal in the Nations League against Cyprus earlier this week, and after also finding the back of the net in the reverse fixture against Latvia, the striker should start once again.

Gharibyan should be supported by Zhirayr Shaghoyan, Artur Serobyan and Narek Grigoryan, with Ugochukwu Iwu and Karlen Hovhannisyan partnering at the base of midfield.

Matrevics; Jurkovskis, Melniks, Cernomordijs, Vientiess, Cirkin; Daskevics, Vapne, Zelenkovs, Ciganiks; Uldrikis

Mishiev; Bandikyan, Harutyunyan, Mkrtchyan, Tiknizyan; Hovhannisyan, Iwu; Grigoryan, Serobyan, Shaghoyan; Gharibyan

Latvia have scored in each of their last three matches, and while we expect them to continue that streak, Armenia demonstrated their superiority on matchday one and should have enough to win again.

#1642. Opinion: England international suggests Liverpool could soon have the best player in the world

Liverpool want to return to the pinnacle of football, and for that they need the best players on the planet.

Richard Hughes was very much motivated by this philosophy. It's why he spent so lavishly as the sporting director of the club.

He wanted to bring in the best players on the market. He did that. On paper he was successful. He secured Bradley Barcola, Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz.

Not to mention other players for whom there was a lot of competition for as well. This includes Milos Kerkez, Jeremy Jacquet, Hugo Ekitike and Giorgi Mamardashvili.

Now aside from the notable exceptions like Ekitike and Jacquet, it's true that so far the aforementioned players have not lived up to their hype.

But transfers are judged in the long-term, not the short-term.

Julian Ward is overseeing a major reshuffleHughes has left behind a bit of a disjointed squad. Ward's job is now to fix that as Liverpool's new sporting director. It's not going to be easy. But the good thing is that the spine of the team is strong. You can comfortably build a team around Isak, Wirtz, Ekitike, Jacquet and Barcola. These are players who could become superstars and who absolutely have what it takes to be world-beaters. On top of that it's important to mention how smartly Liverpool recruited at youth level. Ifeanyi Ndukwe already looks like an incredible value for money. Mor Talla Ndiaye could prove to be the same. Let's not forget about Lucca Brughmanns and Samuel Martinez either who are very highly regarded in their respective age-groups.

By Matt Law | 13 Nov 2026 13:48, Last updated: 13 Nov 2026 13:50

Manchester United are reportedly considering making a move for Como attacker Nico Paz during next summer's transfer window.

The 22-year-old has been in excellent form for his Italian club this season, scoring six goals and registering eight assists in 14 appearances in all competitions.

Paz has been outstanding in the Champions League this term, scoring three goals and registering five assists in four appearances, including two goals and an assist in his team's 4-1 success over Man United in the European competition last month.

The Argentina international arrived at Como from Real Madrid in the summer of 2024, and he has represented Cesc Fabregas' side on 89 occasions, scoring 25 goals and registering 25 assists.

Paz has a contract with Como until the summer of 2028, but there has recently been speculation surrounding his future.

According to The Sun, Man United are keeping a close eye on Paz ahead of a potential move during next summer's transfer window.

The report claims that the Red Devils are looking for a new number 10 amid the uncertainty surrounding Bruno Fernandes' future.

Fernandes has allegedly turned down the chance to sign a new contract at Man United due to disagreements over salary and the length of an extension.

Real Madrid do have the option to re-sign Paz for £67m next summer, but Jude Bellingham is the Spanish club's number 10 and will not be pushed out of the team.

Paz is believed to have turned down the chance to return to Bernabeu at the end of the 2025-26 campaign due to concerns over how much playing time he would receive.

The playmaker joined Real Madrid's youth system in 2016 and went on to represent their first team on eight occasions, scoring once, before a move to Como.

The Argentine is also capable of playing off the right and as a false nine but is more comfortable as a central attacking midfielder.

Man United are expected to be active during the January transfer window, although the bulk of their 2027 business will occur at the end of the campaign.

The Red Devils have confirmed Mauricio Pochettino as their new head coach, with the Argentine set to officially take charge of the 20-time English champions on November 18.

#1640. The Brugge issue and a familiar backstory: Why the Tresoldi deal is becoming off-putting

Recently, it’s felt like AC Milan have been set on signing Nicolo Tresoldi in the winter. It may be the easy option, but is it the right one?

At a time when Milan are doing the PR side of things almost perfectly, Tresoldi feels like another easy win. It seems increasingly likely that Francesco Camarda departs in the winter mercato, so why not replace him with another Milanista?

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Replace the boy who was destined to become king with another who seems further down the career line. He’s already scored a senior goal – or three – at San Siro and he’s got attention from all of Europe’s best clubs. However, if the Rossoneri came knocking, would he be able to say no to his boyhood club?

Well, here is the alternative view: maybe they shouldn’t knock at all.

Now, it’s unpopular to suggest that Tresoldi isn’t the right man, but stick with us here, especially after reports today. If you’ve not seen, Club Brugge have made a statement in the Belgian outlet Het Laatste Nieuws that they won’t be selling him in January.

It’s a ‘club policy’ and even for €60-70 million, he won’t be leaving Belgium. We’ve seen these kinds of statements become pointless in the past and this could become one of them. However, that’s not really the important thing here.

Instead, it’s that Tresoldi has now entered a new bracket. €50m in January is steep, but it’s workable. Ultimately, we’re not in record-breaking territory. Taking that €10-20m step upwards, though, that’s where we enter that territory. There’s also a possibility that more would be needed, too.

It’s a figure that Gerry Cardinale may not be afraid to spend. In fact, reports would have you believe that he really loves Tresoldi and sees him as a perfect addition to a strong frontline roster. However, that’s a lot of money on two strikers in one season.

Then, you’ve also got negotiations with Brugge to deal with. Historically, the Diavolo have found it difficult to close deals with them and with Tresoldi, it’ll be harder than ever, especially after the Ardon Jashari situation.

With the figures being discussed too, you can only imagine how small the margins will be.

Then, you have maybe the most difficult factor. Tresoldi, taking romanticism out of it, has only performed in, with respect, sub-tier leagues. Now, that’s not to take away from his records; scoring-wise, he’s been phenomenal and he’s matched it in the Champions League.

However – and it’s a big however – we’ve already seen that it doesn’t always translate. For example, look at Charles De Ketelaere, but that’s not the real parallel here.

Here, we head to the parallel. In the summer just gone, Milan hired a new Portuguese coach, who initially faced a few questions. After an up-and-down first half of the season, they find themselves in need of a statement January window and stumble upon a boyhood fan of the Rossoneri.

Said fan is banging goals in for fun in a league outside of Europe’s top five, but there’s no need to panic as he’s performing in the Champions League, even against the biggest teams. So, the Rossoneri make the plunge.

Six months later, they try to sell him and a year after that, he’s on loan at Porto, with an €18m buy clause sitting in his deal, unlikely to be touched. Of course, that’s Santiago Gimenez.

There are differences between them, of course, but the formula has already been tried and the results speak for themselves. Trying it again, whilst enticing for the same romantic reasons as Gimenez’s arrival, may not be the answer.

Yes, Gimenez had issues with selection and injuries and eventually, both together. Nevertheless, even without these problems, it was a rushed deal and the Diavolo are going to be the ones paying for that rush next season.

The point here isn’t to discredit the Mexican, but rather suggest that rushing to sign a romantic connection isn’t always the best way to spend big money. It’s about balance, which is why another striker signing like Nicolas Füllkrug wouldn’t be ideal.

Denying that Tresoldi could become a great would be naive, but it would also be as bad to ignore the reasons why the deal is becoming more of a gamble. At €50m, it makes sense, but we’re entering an echelon of deals that requires serious consideration.

In January, Milan would probably have to spend upwards of €70m and that wouldn’t guarantee them Champions League football. Nothing really will offer complete assurances in football; few things – if anything – are guaranteed. Yet, for that fee, it would be expected and you’re still not really addressing the issues within the squad completely.

To do that, Cardinale would have to spend at least another €30-40m to satisfy the fanbase and that’s unreasonable halfway through a season.

So, diversifying the money across the team and then reassessing in the summer may be the best route forward. After all, with this increased price demand, you’re hardly going to be paying more in the summer – and if their demands reach that amount, you’re voicing new questions.

With Markus Krösche also coming in, the January mercato will be one where everything has to be considered carefully and judgements will be made before February 1 rolls around. Spending so heavily on one target may also be an early and unnecessary strike on his record, if it doesn’t work.

For many, Tresoldi made sense in January because he’d be an investment at an investment price. Now, you’re looking at a major budget depletion for a striker who has yet to become a senior international and/or a regular goalscorer in one of Europe’s top five leagues.

The romantic side of it is great; it’s difficult not to fall for that. Financially, though, signing Tresoldi is becoming a tougher sell and that’s where we might have to start listening to the brain rather than the heart.

#1639. Opinion: Arne Slot axed Liverpool star who is perfect for Andoni Iraola

Arne Slot's time as Liverpool's manager was fairly mixed.

He won the Premier League title during his first season in charge but then, just a year later, he was relieved of his duties.

Most fans wanted his sacking to occur months earlier but, Fenway Sports Group chose to stick by him and, luckily, he managed to get his men to qualify for the Champions League.

His fifth-place finish was clearly miles away from where Liverpool actually needed to be which is why Andoni Iraola was brought in.

And, while a lot of people thought his time at Anfield would be smooth-sailing, there are still a lot of changes he needs to make before his team are properly ready to compete for silverware again.

The main issues that need to be rectified are the performances of some players with the January transfer window the best way for them to fix the issues that they're suffering with.

But, while Slot was in charge, he had the answer to one of Iraola's main problems but, instead of keeping him around, he chose to move him on with fans now wondering why that decision was ever made.

Liverpool must figure out what they're doing with their midfield

Liverpool's main problem area among their first-team squad at the moment is their midfield.

They currently have four options to choose from as their number sixes and, while Alexis Mac Allister and Trey Nyoni have put in some solid performances, Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch have both failed to do the same.

The duo were the two midfielders offered long-term contracts by FSG last season with each of them being handed bumper new deals.

Clearly, Liverpool expected them to be their regular midfield duo but, that has been far from the case.

Mac Allister and Nyoni have both performed far better than their teammates and, it feels like they should have been the ones given new contracts instead.

However, that isn't what happened and now, Iraola and Julian Ward seem to be stuck between a rock and a hard place.

So many positions within Liverpool's squad still need upgrading but, if Slot and Richard Hughes had kept one player they sold in the 2025-26 summer window, they'd have one less position to worry about.

Tyler Morton would have been perfect for Andoni Iraola

As mentioned, Liverpool's clear-out last season was taken differently depending on who you asked.

Some people believed that selling players such as Luis Diaz, Tyler Morton and Jarell Quansah was the best thing to do.

But, looking back now, all three of them had incredible campaigns last season and each of them would have been a huge help to Slot.

And, of the lot, Morton is probably the one that Liverpool wish they didn't let go, especially since he's the perfect defensive midfielder for Iraola's system.

Not only can he win duels, keep his line and add extra stability to a team but, he can also create chances and score them if needed.

Alongside all this, he's also a really hard-working central midfielder so, the fact that each of these skills line up perfectly with Iraola's system is a real kick in the teeth.

Obviously, what's done is done and these things can't be changed now but, in hindsight, selling a Liverpool-born midfielder who wanted nothing else but to play for his childhood club was maybe not the Reds' best idea.

That is, especially when they already knew that their midfield was going to be a problem for them.

#1638. Michael Carrick facing the sack at Man United: Mauricio Pochettino the frontrunner to replace beleaguered boss - but chiefs face splashing out £7MILLION for former Spurs and Chelsea coach

Published: 18:04 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 02:44 EST, 10 November 2026

Michael Carrick is facing the sack with Manchester United bosses leaning towards installing a new head coach during the international break.

Carrick’s position has become increasingly precarious after United dropped into the relegation zone despite salvaging a 4-4 draw against Aston Villa at Old Trafford on Sunday.

It left the 45-year-old with just one win from 10 Premier League games this season – United’s worst start since Sir Alex Ferguson replaced Ron Atkinson 40 years ago.

Mauricio Pochettino has emerged as a new frontrunner to replace Carrick. The Argentine is currently in charge of the US national team, but his contract includes a £7million release clause.

Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann, who were both under consideration when United gave Carrick more time to turn the season around following a 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth last month, could also be in contention.

In the three games since then, Carrick’s side lost at Chelsea, staged a remarkable comeback to beat Roma in the Champions League in midweek and then fought back again to draw with Villa.

Michael Carrick is likely to be sacked from his role as Manchester United manager during the international break

It is understood that United officials have not made a final decision, though there is expectation that there will be a new boss in place after the international break

Although it’s understood that no final decision has been reached over Carrick’s future and insiders say that speculation over his sacking is premature, the expectation within Old Trafford is that a new man will be in charge for the visit to Anfield a week on Sunday.

Carrick replaced Ruben Amorim in mid-January and the former United midfielder was handed a two-year contract in May after guiding United to a third-place finish and qualification for the Champions League, losing just two of his 17 games as head coach.

But this season has unravelled alarmingly for United with his three wins in 15 games in all competitions coming at home to newly-promoted Ipswich in the Premier League as well as Sabah of Azerbaijan and Roma in the Champions League.

Asked after Sunday’s chaotic draw with Villa if he would consider quitting, a defiant Carrick said: ‘That's not going to happen.

‘We’re in November. I don’t like this situation and where we are. But we can do something about it. I'm quite clear with what direction the club needs to go in, and it's got to win games.’

Sacking Carrick would leave United searching for their eighth permanent manager or head coach since Ferguson retired 13-and-a-half years ago.

Pochettino was strongly linked with the job when Erik ten Hag was appointed in 2022 and again when the Dutchman was sacked two years later.

The 54-year-old has extensive Premier League experience at Tottenham, Chelsea and Southampton and was also in charge at Paris Saint-Germain.

Current US boss - and former Tottenham and Chelsea manager - Mauricio Pochettino has emerged as the frontrunner to replace Carrick

Howe was previously seen as the favourite but it’s understood there has been no contact between United and the former Newcastle boss.

It would cost United around £3million in compensation to appoint the 48-year-old under the terms of his departure from St James’s Park in July.

Nagelsmann is available after leaving his role as head coach of the German national team in the summer when they were eliminated from the World Cup following a penalty shootout defeat by Paraguay in the round of 32.

#1637. Report: €100m wonderkid on Liverpool's shortlist, he's already been scouted

Liverpool have a lot of problems to solve among their first-team squad.

At the moment, the Reds are just about getting by with the players that they have at their disposal.

However, with so many of Liverpool's contracts set to expire in June 2027, another rebuild feels like its on the cards.

Obviously, this is far from ideal as, over £600 million has been spent on new players by the Anfield outfit already.

But, in order to keep up with their rivals, huge amounts of money now need to be spent each term with the latest rumour to emerge from Anfield being no different.

Liverpool have added Luka Vuskovic back onto their transfer shortlist

The improvement of Liverpool's defence was one of their main focuses in the summer.

The Anfield outfit had a lot of work to do with players such as Dominik Szoboszlai and Curtis Jones being used as right-backs.

And, while they performed fairly well, it's been clear to see how much of a difference having someone such as Ronald Araujo who can actually play there naturally has helped the Reds out.

They're now much more defensively sound and, even though Araujo isn't the only reason for that, he's certainly a big part of it.

However, with the contracts of Virgil van Dijk and Joe Gomez set to expire in June 2027, more change could be afoot.

That is, especially if this latest update from Florian Plettenberg is to be believed.

"Liverpool have Luka Vuskovic on their shortlist for next summer. The 19 y/o top defender is being monitored regularly," he wrote.

"His contract at Brighton is valid until 2031. No release clause will be available next summer. Current price valuation: around €100m (+/-).

"Vuskovic is very happy under Fabian Hürzeler. However, his dream is to join Real Madrid one day."

Luka Vuskovic could have been signed by Liverpool last season

Last term, Vuskovic was on loan to Hamburger SV from Tottenham.

And, even though he was only 18 years old, he was one of their best players.

The performances he was putting in caused interest from across the globe to emerge with some talk of Spurs even keeping hold of him.

Liverpool were one of the teams linked with an interest in the Croatian but, in the end, he joined Brighton for around £46 million.

And, even though some people believed that the Seagull's overpaid, he's quickly proven the doubters wrong.

Now, the Premier League outfit are wanting around €100 million (£83.5 million) to allow him to leave.

Liverpool always seem to figure out that they want a player after they become expensive and, clearly, their desire for Vuskovic is no different.

Here's hoping that, if Liverpool do end up wanting to sign him, that they can knock a few million off the total.

#1636. GdS: ‘Modric of the defence’ – Milan’s chances of landing van Dijk next summer increase

AC Milan have been incredibly interested in a move for Virgil van Dijk in recent years and the opportunity to do so may now have arrived.

Last summer, Gerry Cardinale hoped to sign van Dijk, with just a year left on his deal. However, the timing was not right and the American couldn’t make it work. Yet, that wasn’t the end of the interest and things could heat up in the early stages of next year.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

As Gazzetta dello Sport wrote this morning (seen below), it’s not the first opening that the Rossoneri have had with van Dijk, but it’s perhaps their biggest yet. For the first time, he’s cast doubt on his Liverpool future, with his current deal set to expire at the end of the season.

Speaking yesterday, he admitted that it would be ‘fine’ if there was a renewal offer made, but if not, he had no issue heading elsewhere.

Cardinale has been obsessed with the idea of adding the imposing Dutchman to his Diavolo defence for some time now, even trying to sign him in the summer. However, the terms of a deal weren’t right then.

Andoni Iraola hasn’t shown a strong determination to tie van Dijk down to a new deal, so the Dutchman would be free to discuss a new home in the early parts of 2027.

Milan wouldn’t be alone in their interest in a move, though. Interest from Turkey – Galatasaray, Fenerbahce and Trabzonspor – is present, as are Saudi Arabian clubs. So, it will be dependent on whether the Dutchman prioritises money or his childhood passion.

He fell in love watching Alessandro Nesta and Paolo Maldini, and now the time may come to emulate them as long as the foundations are right. So, the Rossoneri must return to the Champions League, as well as adding some other key players.

Nevertheless, his arrival would be compared to Luka Modric in defence, an elite player whose reputation is among the best of his peers. He could be the core part of a new defence for the Diavolo.

#1635. Chelsea are great entertainers but possess clear weakness

Chelsea are promising to be this season’s Premier League entertainers and yet manager Xabi Alonso seemingly believes less is more when it comes to possession.

Alonso has started with two wins from two league games in charge of Chelsea, with his team scoring seven goals and conceding five. So far, it has been a lot of fun – if not entirely convincing.

But perhaps the most significant numbers are around how much – or how little – Chelsea are having the ball. Having finished their 3-2 victory over Fulham with 38.11 per cent of possession, Chelsea had just 25.6 per cent in the 4-3 success over Brighton and Hove Albion and successfully completed 146 passes. Both were their lowest figures on record in the Premier League.

“The data is not important,” Alonso said. “It’s how you play and what we can do better. I don’t say ‘today we need to have 60 per cent or 20 per cent’. I never talk about those things. It’s about how to prepare, how to be more competitive.”

Chelsea’s third goal against Brighton, scored in the 32nd minute, best summed up the London club under Alonso to date. It took the home side three passes to go from the edge of their own penalty area to João Pedro scoring against his former club.

Jorrel Hato passed the ball to Morgan Rogers, he then released Hato down the left and the wing-back slid the ball across for João Pedro to finish. It was a devastating counter-attack and should have put Chelsea on course for a much easier win.

Joao Pedro finishes off a deadly Chelsea counter-attack and gives the Blues a 3-0 lead 🔥 pic.twitter.com/wAr0ckIgXJ

“After 30 minutes, we are 3-0 and probably, in that moment, we have played too much the result,” Alonso said. “It’s quite normal, it happens in many teams. I am sure in the future we can manage it better.”

It is one thing outscoring Fulham and a depleted Brighton team without having the ball, but can Chelsea do that against the bigger and better teams? We will get an early indicator in the next game against Arsenal at the Emirates.

Alonso’s approach has some similarities to the way in which Antonio Conte set up his Chelsea title-winning team. Just as Conte converted Victor Moses into an effective right wing-back, Alonso started Pedro Neto there on Sunday.

After Roméo Lavia had opened the scoring, it was Neto who grabbed Chelsea’s second goal against Brighton by drifting into the penalty area to finish from Rogers’s low cross.

"It's a nightmare for the goalkeeper!"Bart Verbruggen and Mats Wieffer's collision leads to Romeo Lavia scoring his first goal for Chelsea ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/q5awbdwVV0

"Pedro Neto Pounces!"Morgan Rogers goes past his defender before sliding the ball across to Neto! 💥 pic.twitter.com/WHZCIGsOLl

But whereas Conte’s team gave up little at the back, Alonso’s Chelsea are yet to balance their effective transitional play with shutting out their opponents.

Neto was partly to blame for Brighton’s first goal, as he missed a challenge in the build-up to Malick Yalcouyé’s brilliant volley. Making his Chelsea debut, goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez could do nothing to stop it and can expect to be kept busy this season if things do not change.

“I have come here to challenge and to try and win the Premier League,” Martínez said. “I know the talent we have up front. I try to bring that solidity at the back.”

"Yalcouye with a sumptuous volley!"Malick Yalcouye puts Brighton on the scoreboard with a venomous volley 😳 pic.twitter.com/8UeeyvPjUw

Conte’s Chelsea had N’Golo Kanté to mop up in midfield and that is an area of the pitch that is causing Alonso some difficulties. Manchester City target Enzo Fernández was once again left out of the squad and Moisés Caicedo was not deemed fit enough to start.

Caicedo was eventually thrown on when Chelsea were trying to stop Brighton completing a remarkable comeback, but he was quickly forced off again with an injury. The club have been exploring a move for Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara and that need looks even more pressing now.

“We want the best for the team and that’s why we took a decision [on Fernández] against Luton and today,” Alonso said. “What’s going to develop? We’re not sure. We can prepare. We are preparing for all the scenarios. But I assure you that whatever happens, from Wednesday [when the transfer window is shut] we’ll have a good enough squad to compete in all the Premier League games.”

Chelsea’s new set-piece coach Austin MacPhee had celebrated Lavia’s goal, which came partly as a result of a corner but owed more to a mistake from Brighton goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen.

MacPhee, however, will not have liked Brighton’s second-half goals. It was from a short corner that the visitors managed to work the ball to Pascal Gross and his cross was diverted into his own net by João Pedro.

Joao Pedro puts Pascal Groß's cross into his own net and Brighton have brought it back to 3-2 👀 pic.twitter.com/maBMwVu3DC

Gross’s headed third goal also came at the end of a set-piece, but, fortunately for Chelsea, it was in the sixth minute of added time and Cole Palmer had already made the points safe for the home team before then.

Palmer had done little to impress watching England head coach Thomas Tuchel until he picked up the ball in the 74th minute, shrugged off two Brighton challenges and produced a brilliant finish to beat Verbruggen.

Cole Palmer finishes EXPERTLY to give Chelsea their two-goal cushion back 💥 pic.twitter.com/6xI9W8xe2q

Fabian Hürzeler, the Brighton manager, said his team “dominated” the game, but acknowledged: “I think if you spend so much money on these kinds of players, like Rogers, Palmer or João [Pedro], then, of course, a team like Chelsea can rely on this individual quality. And they showed it in certain moments of the game.”

Palmer, João Pedro and Rogers are clearly going to be a huge problem for Chelsea’s opponents. But Alonso’s team cannot rely on having to score three or four goals to win games. And they might need to have a bit more of the ball.

"The game today was a special game for me." João Pedro says he was happy with his performance for Chelsea against Brighton 🔵 pic.twitter.com/fWSqWo7ert

6 - João Pedro today was the sixth player (and first for Chelsea) to score a goal, assist a goal, and score an own goal in the same Premier League game, and first since Tottenham Hotspur's Son Heung-min against Man City in December 2023.Eventful. pic.twitter.com/xRVjqkOY9D

Brighton meanwhile confirmed their place in the Conference League group stages with a 4-0 aggregate win over Tromso.

Enzo Fernandez was not involved in Chelsea’s squad against Luton on Thursday and has been heavily linked with a move to Manchester City. Brighton began their Premier League campaign in emphatic style as they thrashed Aston Villa 4-0 at home seven days ago. They are also without Yankuba Minteh, who has been linked with a move to Liverpool this summer but is unavailable due to injury.

“When the window is closed I demand from him [Minteh] that he is fully committed to this club,” Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler said. “There are dreams and wishes for players, but in the end we always need to figure out what is best for the club.

The last few years have shown that the whole environment gave him a lot of trust and belief that he is capable of having this progress. It is always a give and take and he has gotten a lot from us.”

Brighton won both Premier League meetings last season, winning 3-1 in this fixture last September. Brighton have won five of their last eight top-flight meetings with Chelsea. Team news from Stamford Bridge to follow shortly.
